text:
incident-bot: [ALERT] Serving runtime: multiple pods reporting OOM + CUDA illegal memory access on node gpu-reef-07 (severity: high)

jess: paging @oncall-matt @sahil — gpu-reef-07 is spiking device-address faults and containers are restarting. Can you grab triage? :rotating_light:

oncall-matt: on it. seeing repeated kernel messages in node dmesg: `NVIDIA: CUDA illegal memory access` and `invalid device address` along with a few panics in the runtime.

sahil: curious if this is the same pagewalk race we've seen before or new. any pattern on model size/seq len?

jess: started after a model rollout ~2m before alert. Affected pods: inference-prod-1/2/3 on that node. All running the llm-serving:release-2026-03.

cust-support: customer-impact: 2 high-traffic tenants reported 503s and degraded latency for ~11 minutes. Some requests retried, but overall error rate spike.

nyla: past incidents had a kernel translation/cache race causing misaligned device addresses. attaching dmesg snippet: 
```
[3343219988.123] nvidia: module: CUDA illegal memory access at 0x7f8a1c00
[3343219988.124] nvidia: gpu-addr: pagewalk fail, translation fault
[3343219989.010] containerd: inference-prod-1: killed by signal 11 (SEGV)
[3343219990.001] runtime: device pointer invalid, attempt to map stale page
```

jess: good. also attaching kube logs from pod inference-prod-1: 
```
E0307 12:33:09.456 1 runtime.go:213] failed to run model chunk: CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS
E0307 12:33:09.457 1 server.go:89] restarting container due to runtime error
```

oncall-matt: immediate mitigation plan: 1) cordon gpu-reef-07 2) drain non-critical pods 3) move inference traffic via routing rule to dedicated fallback pool 4) roll back the model rollout to previous stable image 5) escalate to kernel/driver team if faults persist.

sahil: agree. also we should enable evict-on-failure for the runtime to avoid noisy restarts, and disable prefetching/large page mappings for the affected model as a temporary config.

deploy-bot: Rolling back deployment inference-service -> llm-serving:release-2026-02 (requested by jess). Start: 3343220050

ops-sre: cordon command issued: `kubectl cordon gpu-reef-07` (done). Draining low-priority pods now with `--delete-local-data --force` in batches.

cust-support: notifying customers: email template ready, sending to affected tenants now (IDs: T-845, T-662). ETA for full mitigation 20-30m.

nyla: collecting traces and kernel oops: I'm starting a full capture and will upload to the incident doc. If we can repro with smaller job, we should.

oncall-matt: noticed pattern: faults correlate with long sequences (>2k tokens) and frequent kv-cache flushes. Could be a race in KV pointer lifetime in the runtime when model weights are sharded.

sahil: if it's pointer lifetime, a quick fix is to force sync on cache eviction and avoid async unmap. I'll push a canary hotfix to a single replica on fallback pool for validation.

jess: @sahil please coordinate with @deploy-bot to canary the hotfix and keep us posted. Also remember to capture full kernel oops and GPU qemu metrics.

deploy-bot: Canary deploy started: llm-serving-hotfix-2026-03-canary -> 1 replica in fallback pool at 3343220300

oncall-matt: after cordon/drain and rollback, error rate dropped to baseline. no new illegal memory access logs in last 6m on other nodes.

cust-support: customer update: services restored for T-662, T-845 showing partial recovery; ongoing retries cleared most errors.

nyla: kernel team pinged and opening internal ticket KERN-1629 with attached oops and trace. marking suspected cause: user-level DMA pointer race with translation cache invalidation.

sahil: quick followups — add an automatic fallback routing rule to route high-seqlen requests to instances with KV-cache disabled. This should reduce risk until we have a driver patch.

jess: agreed. Ops — keep node cordoned until kernel/driver update. We'll schedule maintenance for kernel/driver rollout with vendor.

ops-sre: node remaining cordoned. plan to repro in staging with identical workload and memory pressure. If repro succeeds, prepare kernel-module patch + runtime guard.

incident-bot: Incident update: severity -> high -> mitigated (partial). Next update in 30m or when kernel team posts findings.

jess: summary for postmortem: root cause suspected kernel/driver race causing misaligned device address translations under certain KV-cache eviction patterns. Impact: ~11-14m of elevated 5xx for two tenants, rollbacks + cordon mitigations applied. Action items created: isolate repro (nyla), runtime guard (sahil), vendor kernel engagement (jess).

oncall-matt: handing off to next oncall @sahil for monitoring / vendor coordination. I'll leave the incident channel.

sahil: taking over. will keep this thread updated and push progress to incident doc. :thumbsup:

cust-support: closing customer-facing incident notes once kernel patch ETA received.

jess: thanks everyone. good triage.
